user.title: HDG Bavaria Boiler Setup
user.description: Configure the connection to your HDG Bavaria Boiler.

data.host_ip: Boiler's Host IP Address or Hostname
data.device_alias: Alias for the Boiler (optional, for device & entity names)

data_description.host_ip: The IP address or hostname of your HDG Boiler (e.g., '192.168.1.100' or 'hdg-boiler.local').
data_description.device_alias: An optional, user-friendly name for this boiler in Home Assistant. If left empty, a default name will be used.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the HDG Boiler. Please check the IP address and ensure the boiler is reachable and the API is enabled.
error.unknown: An unknown error occurred during setup.
error.alias_already_exists: This device alias is already in use by another HDG Boiler. Please choose a unique alias if you provide one.

abort.already_configured: This HDG Boiler (based on host IP) is already configured.
abort.host_ip_required: The boiler's IP address or hostname is required.

data_description.device_alias: An optional, user-friendly name for this boiler in Home Assistant. If left empty, a default name will be used.
data_description.scan_interval_group_1: Interval for polling the most important real-time data (e.g., temperatures, status). Default: {default_scan_interval_group_1}s.
data_description.scan_interval_group_2: Interval for polling general status information. Default: {default_scan_interval_group_2}s.
data_description.scan_interval_group_3: Interval for polling configuration and counter data (Part 1). Default: {default_scan_interval_group_3}s.
data_description.scan_interval_group_4: Interval for polling configuration and counter data (Part 2). Default: {default_scan_interval_group_4}s.
data_description.scan_interval_group_5: Interval for polling configuration and counter data (Part 3). Default: {default_scan_interval_group_5}s.
data_description.log_level: Sets the verbosity of logs for this integration. 'DEBUG' is very verbose and useful for troubleshooting. 'INFO' is the standard for normal operation.
data_description.advanced_logging: Enables additional INFO-level logs for important actions (e.g., setting values, API request/response summaries), even when the main integration log level is set to `INFO`. Useful for tracking key operations without enabling full `DEBUG` logging, which can be very verbose.
data_description.source_timezone: The timezone in which the boiler provides its time data (e.g., 'Europe/Berlin'). This is important for correct interpretation of date/time values from the boiler.
data_description.api_timeout: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait for a response from the boiler for any API request. A higher value can help with unstable networks but may lead to longer waits. Range: {min_api_timeout}-{max_api_timeout}s.
data_description.connect_timeout: The maximum time (in seconds) to wait for a connection to be established with the boiler. Range: {min_connect_timeout}-{max_connect_timeout}s.
data_description.polling_preemption_timeout: The maximum time (in seconds) a low-priority polling request is allowed to run if a higher-priority request (e.g., a setting change) is queued. A lower value ensures faster response to setting changes but may lead to more frequent interruptions with slow boiler responses. This value must be a whole number. Range: {min_polling_preemption_timeout}-{max_polling_preemption_timeout}s.
data_description.recently_set_poll_ignore_window_s: Time window (in seconds) to ignore updates for values that have been recently set via Home Assistant. This prevents the integration from immediately overwriting a user's change with an old value from the boiler. Default: {default_ignore_window}s, Range: {min_ignore_window}-{max_ignore_window}s.
data_description.log_level_threshold_for_connection_error: The number of consecutive connection failures after which the logging level for connection errors escalates. For example, if set to 5, the first 4 connection errors will be logged as INFO, and the 5th and subsequent errors will be logged as ERROR. Non-connection API errors will be logged as WARNING after this threshold. Range: 1-60
data_description.error_threshold: The number of consecutive errors before the integration raises an `UpdateFailed` error and stops trying to reconnect for a while. Range: {min_error_threshold}-{max_error_threshold}.
data_description.log_level_threshold_for_preemption_error: The number of consecutive preemption errors before logging escalates. Below this, errors are logged as INFO. At or above, they are logged as WARNING. Range: {min_preemption_threshold}-{max_preemption_threshold}.
data_description.fallback_ping_interval: The interval in seconds to ping the host when it is considered offline. A successful ping will trigger an immediate refresh attempt. Range: {min_fallback_ping_interval}-{max_fallback_ping_interval}s, Default: {default_fallback_ping_interval}s.

error.scan_interval_invalid_range_min_max: Scan interval must be between 15 and 86400 seconds.
error.api_timeout_invalid_range_min_max: API Timeout must be between {min_api_timeout} and {max_api_timeout} seconds.
error.polling_preemption_timeout_invalid_range: Polling Preemption Timeout must be between {min_polling_preemption_timeout} and {max_polling_preemption_timeout} seconds.
error.log_level_threshold_invalid_range_min_ma: The Connection Error Threshold must be between {min_log_level_threshold} and {max_log_level_threshold}.

set_node_value.name: Set HDG Boiler Node Value
set_node_value.description: Sets a specific node value on the HDG boiler. The node_id must be configured in the integration's internal HDG_NODE_SETTER_CONFIG for validation.

node_id.name: Node ID
node_id.description: The ID of the HDG Node to set (e.g., '6022').

value.name: Value
value.description: The value to send to the node.

get_node_value.name: Get HDG Boiler Node Value
get_node_value.description: Retrieves the current value of a specific node from the integration's internal state.

node_id.name: Node ID
node_id.description: The ID of the HDG Node to retrieve (e.g., '22003').
